summary: Extensions should combine process effort with external outcome evidence, monitor calibration, and treat abnormal compute as a risk signal rather than prestige.

items.text: Display a two-axis review matrix: normalized compute effort on one axis and independent safety-net evidence on the other. Only the evidence axis can authorize acceptance.
Publish calibration reports by task class showing whether the fingerprint predicts reviewer findings, rework, or escaped defects, and retire dimensions that add no predictive value.
Treat sudden retry explosions, repeated denied tool calls, or unusual model upgrades as anomaly signals that tighten authority and trigger review.
When compute is externally sponsored, expose the normalized fingerprint in the contribution statement but explicitly separate recognition from quality and governance.
